newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NATO's Solana, on Russian holiday, meets Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana, on Russian holiday, meets Nemtsov.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana met Russian reform champion Boris Nemtsov on Monday in the first of a series of unofficial talks while on holiday in Russia.
Solana toured Red Square with his wife and two children on a cloudy morning before meeting First Deputy Prime Minister Nemtsov.

He is expected to hold further informal talks while in Russia, which was fiercely opposed to NATO's expansion into Eastern Europe but tacitly accepted it earlier this year by agreeing to a pact with the alliance.
Nemtsov said Moscow still felt threatened by the West and saw a link between its economic and military security.
"We must create a single European economy and I think that the anti-dumping measures taken by the European Union are totally at odds with the needs of a united Europe," he said after the talks.
Nemtsov was reiterating Russia's anger at trade barriers imposed by the EU against Russian goods which it says are dumped at low prices.
The former Spanish foreign minister thrashed out the difficult security pact with Moscow before NATO issued invitations to several former Warsaw Pact members last month.
Nemtsov stressed that Moscow would not accept any moves by NATO towards incorporating the Baltic states -- three former Soviet republics clamouring for membership of the alliance.

Interfax news agency quoted Solana as saying the trip, during which he is also due to meet Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, was purely personal and aimed at establishing "not just formal, but close personal ties" with Russian leaders.
